newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Yahoo! advertisers rise to 700.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Yahoo! advertisers rise to 700.

text.p: Yahoo! Inc president and chief executive officer Tim Koogle said the company now has 700 advertisers, up from 550 at the end of 1996, and still expects to achieve its target of operating profits in 1998.
Koogle told Reuters in an interview that the company sold advertising on roughly 20 percent of its total page views in the first quarter.
Earlier the company posted first quarter earnings per share which topped Wall Street estimates.
The company said in a statement that the average number of daily page views in the month of March 1997 was more than 30 million, a 50 percent jump from 20 million in December.
"We've said we will reach operating profitability in 1998," Koogle said after a conference call with analysts, repeating the company's objective stated in earlier financial meetings.

Yahoo! said its cash, cash equivalents and investments declined to $94.9 million at March 31, compared with $102.3 million as of December 31, 1996, which reflects in part a one-time payment of $5 million to Netscape Communications Corp to license its brand and trademarks as part of a multi-year agreement to supply Netscape Guide by Yahoo!.
The guide opens a new delivery channel to Yahoo!. Yahoo! will program, produce, operate and run ad sales for the navigation service. The guide is due to be launched in the current quarter.

Analysts estimate Yahoo! is also spending roughly $1 million a quarter on its share of the premier position on the Internet search button on Netscape, which it shares with other rival search engines. Koogle declined to give a specific figure.

"For us it's like last year, it's a combination of cash plus some co-promotion," he said. "I think the folks doing consensus projections on us had budgeted it in as what we spent last year, plus a 'little cost of living increase."
"We're within that range, so its no surprise to anybody," said Koogle.
Koogle added that with the company having placed advertising on around 20 percent of the total number of pages viewed, there was still a lot of room to sell further space.
"There's a lot of headroom," he said.
The Yahoo! CEO said barter advertising remained at an "insignificant amount" and remains at the lower end of the five to 10 percent range it has historically been.

He said Yahoo! will focus some of its selling efforts on major multinational customers and deals like the global Internet advertising program which International Business Machines Corp has placed with Yahoo!
